A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of the genetics of alcoholism in the development of alcohol dependence and related problems in a large, prospective sample of individuals.
the risk for alcoholism in first-degree family members of alcoholics is increased, but the magnitude of risk varies with age, gender, and type of relative.
the risk for alcohol dependence in the offspring of alcohol‐dependent probands (AD) is increased 2‐3‐fold compared with the risk in offspring of controls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified a genetic risk factor for alcohol dependence.
